elements.name: Dataset Discovery and Identification
elements.description: Can a user or system discover and uniquely identify this dataset?

sub_elements.name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, etc.)
sub_elements.evidence: id: https://fairhub.io/datasets/2; doi: 10.57895/fairhub.2
sub_elements.quality_note: Both unique ID and properly formatted DOI present, enabling persistent identification and citation

sub_elements.name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
sub_elements.evidence: title: Artificial Intelligence Ready and Equitable Atlas for Diabetes Insights (AI-READI); description spans lines 10-22 with 800+ characters
sub_elements.quality_note: Clear, descriptive title and comprehensive description explaining dataset purpose, scope (4,000 participants, 3 sites), design (triple-balanced), and multimodal data domains

sub_elements.name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
sub_elements.evidence: keywords: [Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, T2DM, AI-READI, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, multimodal dataset, harmonized data, multi-site study, salutogenesis, FAIR principles, retinal imaging, continuous glucose monitoring, wearable devices, biorepository, biospecimens, triple-balanced sampling, health equity, Bridge2AI, cross-sectional study] - 20 keywords total
sub_elements.quality_note: Excellent keyword coverage (20 keywords) spanning disease domain, methodology, project affiliation, and data types

sub_elements.name: Dataset Landing Page or Platform URL
sub_elements.evidence: page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/2
sub_elements.quality_note: Active, accessible landing page on FAIRhub platform where users can access dataset information and downloads

sub_elements.name: Associated Project or Program
sub_elements.evidence: keywords include 'Bridge2AI'; funders section (lines 178-186) states 'NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI Program' with grant OT2OD032644
sub_elements.quality_note: Clear and explicit association with Bridge2AI program, including grant number and funding details

elements.name: Dataset Access and Retrieval
elements.description: Can the dataset and its associated resources be located, accessed, and downloaded?

sub_elements.name: Access Mechanism Defined
sub_elements.evidence: subsets section (lines 200-222) defines 'Public Access Dataset' (available to public upon license agreement) and 'Controlled Access Dataset' (requires data use agreement)
sub_elements.quality_note: Two-tier access model clearly documented: public access for non-sensitive data, controlled access with DUA for sensitive data (genetic, geographic identifiers)

sub_elements.name: Data Use Agreement Required?
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms (lines 515-527): 'Public access data distributed under Creative Commons Attribution Non-Commercial (CC BY-NC 4.0) license. Controlled access data requires a separate data use agreement with the University of Washington as Licensor.'
sub_elements.quality_note: DUA requirements explicitly stated for each access tier: CC BY-NC 4.0 for public data, institutional DUA for controlled access, with prohibition on re-identification

sub_elements.name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
sub_elements.evidence: line 208: 'Available at https://fairhub.io/datasets/2'; external_resources section (line 643) repeats FAIRhub landing page
sub_elements.quality_note: Direct download platform URL provided (FAIRhub), accessible for registered users

sub_elements.name: File Formats Specified
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats section (lines 530-548): DICOM for imaging, CSV for tabular/time-series, mHealth standard for wearable data, XML for ECG
sub_elements.quality_note: All major file formats explicitly listed with use cases: DICOM (imaging), CSV (surveys, labs, CGM, environmental), mHealth (wearables), XML (ECG)

sub_elements.name: External Links to Similar or Related Datasets
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources section (lines 629-674) includes 9 resources: AI-READI website, documentation portal, FAIRhub page, Bridge2AI program link, NIH RePORTER, data sharing policies, Zenodo archive, BMJ Open protocol publication, Nature Metabolism commentary
sub_elements.quality_note: Comprehensive external resources including project website, documentation, related publications, parent program (Bridge2AI), and NIH grant database

elements.name: Data Reuse and Interoperability
elements.description: Is sufficient information provided to reuse and integrate the dataset with others?

sub_elements.name: License Terms Allow Reuse
sub_elements.evidence: license: CC BY-NC 4.0 (line 25); license_and_use_terms (lines 515-527): 'Permits others to distribute, remix, adapt, build upon this work non-commercially, and license their derivative works on different terms, provided the original work is properly cited'
sub_elements.quality_note: Clear CC BY-NC 4.0 license allowing non-commercial reuse, remixing, and derivative works with proper attribution

sub_elements.name: Data Formats Are Standardized
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats (lines 530-548): DICOM (imaging standard), CSV (widely used tabular), mHealth (wearable device standard), XML (ECG)
sub_elements.quality_note: All formats are industry standards: DICOM (medical imaging), CSV (universal tabular), mHealth (mobile health devices), XML (structured clinical data)

sub_elements.name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
sub_elements.evidence: preprocessing_strategies (lines 440-448): 'OMOP Common Data Model for clinical data', 'DICOM for retinal imaging', 'mHealth standard for wearable device data', 'RxNorm codes for medications', 'ICD-10 codes for diabetes classification'
sub_elements.quality_note: Explicit conformance to multiple standards/ontologies: OMOP CDM (clinical), DICOM (imaging), mHealth (wearables), RxNorm (drugs), ICD-10 (diagnoses)

sub_elements.name: Identifiers Defined for Linking
sub_elements.evidence: No explicit 'identifiers_in_files' or similar field documenting participant IDs, linking keys, or cross-file identifiers
sub_elements.quality_note: Missing: While participant-based structure is implied, no explicit documentation of identifiers for linking across data files or tables

sub_elements.name: Documentation of Processing Tools for Reproducibility
sub_elements.evidence: acquisition_methods (lines 309-388) lists data capture devices and software (REDCap, Dexcom G6, Garmin VivoSmart 5, imaging devices), but no 'software_and_tools' field with processing code repositories or pipelines
sub_elements.quality_note: Partial: Data capture tools documented, but no links to processing code, GitHub repositories, or computational pipelines for reproducibility

elements.name: Ethical Use and Privacy Safeguards
elements.description: Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?

sub_elements.name: IRB or Ethics Review Documented
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews section (lines 588-595): 'Study approved by Institutional Review Board (IRB) of University of Washington (approval number STUDY00016228), with reliance agreements from IRBs of University of Alabama at Birmingham and University of California, San Diego'
sub_elements.quality_note: Comprehensive IRB documentation: approval number (STUDY00016228), lead institution (UW), and reliance agreements from UAB and UCSD

sub_elements.name: Deidentification Method Described
sub_elements.evidence: No 'deidentification_and_privacy.approach' field; sensitive_elements section (lines 610-626) describes what data is in controlled access but not deidentification methods
sub_elements.quality_note: Missing: No explicit deidentification method documented (e.g., HIPAA Safe Harbor, Expert Determination, k-anonymity)

sub_elements.name: Identifiers Removed or Masked
sub_elements.evidence: No 'deidentification_and_privacy.examples_of_identifiers_removed' field; sensitive_elements mentions 5-digit zip code and demographics are in controlled access (lines 619-622) but no list of removed identifiers
sub_elements.quality_note: Missing: No explicit list of identifiers removed, masked, or generalized during deidentification process

sub_elements.name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews (lines 591-595): 'Written informed consent provided by all participants'; human_subject_research (lines 604-607): 'Study involves human subjects research with IRB approval and written informed consent from all participants'
sub_elements.quality_note: Clear statement that written informed consent was obtained from all 4,000 participants, documented in both ethical_reviews and human_subject_research sections

sub_elements.name: Ethical Sourcing Statement Included
sub_elements.evidence: No explicit 'ethics.ethical_position' field; human_subject_research mentions bioethics guidance and Community Advisory Board (lines 601-607) but no formal ethical sourcing statement
sub_elements.quality_note: Partial: Bioethics involvement and Community Advisory Board mentioned, but no structured ethical sourcing statement or ethical position declaration

elements.name: Data Composition and Structure
elements.description: Can the dataset's structure, modality, and population be understood from metadata?

sub_elements.name: Cohort or Population Characteristics Described
sub_elements.evidence: instances section (lines 189-198): 'Individual participants aged 40 and older with and without Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, triple-balanced by self-reported race/ethnicity (Asian, Black, Hispanic, White), T2DM severity (no diabetes, pre-diabetes/lifestyle-controlled, medication-controlled, insulin-controlled), and biological sex (male, female)'
sub_elements.quality_note: Comprehensive population description: age (40+), diabetes status, triple-balanced design across race/ethnicity (4 groups), sex (2 groups), and diabetes severity (4 levels); inclusion/exclusion criteria specified

sub_elements.name: Number of Participants or Samples Reported
sub_elements.evidence: instances section (lines 191-192): 'Target enrollment is 4,000 people'; updates section (lines 571-575) mentions pilot data and progressive releases (v1.0.0, v2.0.0, v3.0.0) toward 4,000 target
sub_elements.quality_note: Clear target sample size (4,000 participants) with interim releases documented; final dataset expected after November 2026 completion

sub_elements.name: Modalities or Data Types Listed
sub_elements.evidence: acquisition_methods section (lines 309-388) lists 12 modalities: surveys/questionnaires, physical measurements, retinal imaging (7 devices), visual function testing, clinical lab testing, ECG, cognitive function (MoCA), peripheral neuropathy assessment, continuous glucose monitoring, physical activity monitoring, environmental monitoring, biospecimens
sub_elements.quality_note: Extensive modality documentation: 10+ data domains covering surveys, clinical measurements, multi-device imaging, wearables, environmental sensors, and biospecimens

sub_elements.name: Conditions or Phenotypes Represented
sub_elements.evidence: instances section (lines 189-198): Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus with severity stratification; subpopulations section (lines 263-272): no diabetes, pre-diabetes/lifestyle-controlled, medication-controlled, insulin-controlled diabetes
sub_elements.quality_note: Clear phenotype stratification: T2DM as primary condition with four severity levels (none, pre-diabetes/lifestyle, medication, insulin) representing disease progression spectrum

sub_elements.name: File Dimensions or Sampling Rates Provided
sub_elements.evidence: acquisition_methods: CGM 'every 5 minutes for 10 days' (lines 365-368), physical activity monitoring '10 days' (lines 370-374), environmental monitoring '10 days' (lines 376-381); imaging devices and test protocols detailed
sub_elements.quality_note: Temporal sampling rates documented: CGM (5-min intervals, 10 days), wearables (10-day monitoring); imaging protocols and cognitive test scoring ranges provided

elements.name: Data Provenance and Version Tracking
elements.description: Can a user determine dataset versions, update history, and provenance?

sub_elements.name: Dataset Version Number Provided
sub_elements.evidence: No top-level 'dataset_version' or 'version' field; updates section mentions v1.0.0, v2.0.0, v3.0.0 (lines 566-575) but no current version specified in metadata header
sub_elements.quality_note: Missing: No explicit dataset version field in metadata, though version history is documented in updates section

sub_elements.name: Version History Documented
sub_elements.evidence: updates section (lines 560-576): 'Pilot data released May 2024. v1.0.0 data through July 31, 2024 released November 2024. v2.0.0 and v3.0.0 released with additional participants. Final dataset expected after completion of enrollment by November 2026'
sub_elements.quality_note: Clear version progression documented: pilot (May 2024), v1.0.0 (Nov 2024, data through July 31), v2.0.0 and v3.0.0 (incremental), final (late 2026)

sub_elements.name: Change Descriptions for Each Version
sub_elements.evidence: updates section (lines 571-575): Each version described with release date and content (e.g., 'v1.0.0 data through July 31, 2024 released November 2024', 'v2.0.0 and v3.0.0 released with additional participants')
sub_elements.quality_note: Version changes documented: pilot testing phase, v1.0.0 cutoff date (July 31, 2024), subsequent versions add participants, final version post-enrollment completion

sub_elements.name: Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated
sub_elements.evidence: updates section (line 569): 'frequency: Periodic releases with ongoing enrollment; final release planned for late 2026'; enrollment window 'July 18, 2023 to November 30, 2026' (lines 292-294)
sub_elements.quality_note: Clear update schedule: periodic releases during enrollment (July 2023 - November 2026), final dataset post-enrollment completion in late 2026

sub_elements.name: Versioned Documentation or External References
sub_elements.evidence: updates section (lines 575-576): 'Dataset versioning implemented with version-specific documentation at https://docs.aireadi.org/'; external_resources (lines 636-639): 'AI-READI Dataset Documentation' at https://docs.aireadi.org/
sub_elements.quality_note: Versioned documentation portal (https://docs.aireadi.org/) provides version-specific guides for each release, ensuring users can access historical documentation

elements.name: Scientific Motivation and Funding Transparency
elements.description: Does the metadata clearly state why the dataset exists and who funded it?

sub_elements.name: Motivation or Rationale for Dataset Creation
sub_elements.evidence: purposes section (lines 49-71) lists three purposes: (1) Understanding T2DM salutogenesis through hypothesis-agnostic, harmonized, multi-domain dataset for AI/ML; (2) Establishing AI/ML data standards and best practices; (3) Addressing demographic inequities through triple-balanced sampling across race/ethnicity, sex, and diabetes severity
sub_elements.quality_note: Comprehensive rationale: scientific (salutogenesis pathways), methodological (AI/ML standards), and ethical (health equity) motivations clearly articulated

sub_elements.name: Primary Research Objective or Task
sub_elements.evidence: intended_uses section (lines 465-494) lists five uses: (1) AI/ML model development for T2DM and salutogenesis (primary), (2) multi-modal T2DM research, (3) health equity research, (4) biomarker discovery, (5) model dataset for AI-ready standards; tasks section (lines 73-91) details ML model development and disease trajectory analysis
sub_elements.quality_note: Primary objective (AI/ML for T2DM salutogenesis) clearly stated with supporting secondary objectives and specific ML tasks (pseudotime manifold analysis, unbiased models)

sub_elements.name: Funding Source or Grant Agency Listed
sub_elements.evidence: funders section (lines 178-186): 'NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI Program, Funded through National Institutes of Health grant OT2OD032644, administered by NIH Office of the Director. Additional support from grants P30DK035816 (Nutrition and Obesity Research Center), UL1TR003096, and Research to Prevent Blindness'
sub_elements.quality_note: Comprehensive funding documentation: primary funder (NIH Common Fund), administering office (NIH Office of the Director), program (Bridge2AI), and additional supporting grants

sub_elements.name: Award Number or Grant ID Present
sub_elements.evidence: funders section (lines 182-183): 'grant OT2OD032644' with additional grants 'P30DK035816', 'UL1TR003096'; NIH RePORTER link (lines 651-654) provides project details for '1OT2OD032644-01'
sub_elements.quality_note: Multiple grant numbers provided: primary grant OT2OD032644 plus supporting grants P30DK035816 (NORC) and UL1TR003096; NIH RePORTER link enables verification

sub_elements.name: Acknowledgement of Platform or Participant Support
sub_elements.evidence: funders section (lines 183-186): 'Total funding in 2022: $5,026,499. Project dates: September 1, 2022 to August 31, 2025'; human_subject_research section (lines 601-607): 'Community Advisory Board of 11 persons with diversity in race and ethnicity contributes to protocol development'
sub_elements.quality_note: Acknowledgements include funding amount ($5M+), project timeline, support from Research to Prevent Blindness, and Community Advisory Board (11 diverse members) contribution

elements.name: Technical Transparency (Data Collection and Processing)
elements.description: Can data collection and processing steps be replicated or understood?

sub_elements.name: Collection Setting or Sites Described
sub_elements.evidence: description (lines 10-22): '3 data collection sites (Birmingham, Alabama; San Diego, California; Seattle, Washington)'; collection_mechanisms (lines 277-281): 'Single study encounter per participant at one of three data collection sites (Birmingham, San Diego, Seattle)'
sub_elements.quality_note: Collection sites explicitly documented: Birmingham AL (UAB), San Diego CA (UCSD), Seattle WA (UW) with institutional affiliations clear from creators and IRB sections

sub_elements.name: Data Capture Method or Device Listed
sub_elements.evidence: acquisition_methods section (lines 309-388) extensively documents devices: REDCap (surveys), Aurora IQ/EIDON/Spectralis/Maestro2/Triton/Cirrus 5000/FLIO (imaging), Electronic Visual Acuity tester (M&S Technology), Topcon KR 800 (autorefraction), Philips Pagewriter TC30 (ECG), MoCA Duo Application (cognitive), Dexcom G6 (CGM), Garmin VivoSmart 5 (activity), custom environmental sensor
sub_elements.quality_note: Comprehensive device documentation: manufacturer names, model numbers, and specific uses for all 10+ data domains (imaging, wearables, clinical instruments, software platforms)

sub_elements.name: Preprocessing or Cleaning Steps Documented
sub_elements.evidence: preprocessing_strategies section (lines 391-448) documents: (1) data standardization/harmonization across sites via REDCap and SOPs, (2) image format conversion (proprietary to DICOM), (3) biospecimen processing protocols, (4) quality control and validation (training, calibration, duplicate measurements), (5) data mapping to standards (OMOP, DICOM, mHealth, RxNorm, ICD-10); cleaning_strategies section (lines 450-462) describes multi-site harmonization
sub_elements.quality_note: Detailed preprocessing documentation: harmonization procedures, format conversions, QC protocols (coordinator training/certification, equipment calibration, duplicate measurements), and standard mappings

sub_elements.name: Open-Source Processing Code Provided
sub_elements.evidence: No 'software_and_tools.preprocessing_code' field; no GitHub repositories, code links, or computational pipeline documentation provided despite extensive tool/device listings
sub_elements.quality_note: Missing: No processing code, GitHub repositories, or computational pipeline documentation provided; would enable full reproducibility of preprocessing and analysis steps

sub_elements.name: External Standards or References Cited
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources section includes peer-reviewed publications: (lines 666-669) 'Protocol Publication (BMJ Open): BMJ Open publication describing study design and protocol (Owsley et al. 2025) https://doi.org/10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449'; (lines 670-674) 'Nature Metabolism Commentary: Overview of AI-READI approach and significance https://doi.org/10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x'
sub_elements.quality_note: Peer-reviewed protocol publications cited: BMJ Open (Owsley et al. 2025, full study design) and Nature Metabolism commentary (approach/significance); enables detailed methodology review

elements.name: Dataset Evaluation and Limitations Disclosure
elements.description: Does the metadata communicate known risks, biases, or dataset limitations?

sub_elements.name: Limitations Section Present
sub_elements.evidence: No explicit 'limitations' field in metadata; limitations discussed within other sections (why_not_representative, discouraged_uses) but not consolidated
sub_elements.quality_note: Missing: No dedicated limitations section; limitations information scattered across sampling_strategies.why_not_representative and discouraged_uses sections

sub_elements.name: Sampling Bias or Representativeness Noted
sub_elements.evidence: sampling_strategies.why_not_representative (lines 237-246): 'The triple-balanced design intentionally over-samples racial/ethnic minority groups and specific diabetes severity groups relative to their population prevalence, to enable unbiased AI/ML model development. Participants are volunteers, introducing volunteer selection bias that may limit generalizability to non-volunteer populations'
sub_elements.quality_note: Explicit acknowledgment of two biases: (1) intentional over-sampling of minorities (not population-representative), (2) volunteer selection bias limiting generalizability to broader population

sub_elements.name: Quality Control or Validation Steps Mentioned
sub_elements.evidence: preprocessing_strategies (lines 426-437): 'Multiple quality control measures including standardized training of study coordinators, equipment calibration, duplicate measurements, and data validation checks in REDCap system. Data managers at each site oversee quality control before uploading to FAIRhub. Practice subjects required before enrolling participants'
sub_elements.quality_note: Comprehensive QC documentation: coordinator training/certification, equipment calibration, duplicate measurements (e.g., BP measured twice), REDCap validation checks, practice subjects, site data manager oversight

sub_elements.name: Known Risks or Use Constraints Listed
sub_elements.evidence: discouraged_uses section (lines 495-512) lists three constraints: (1) 'Uses during ongoing enrollment without awareness of limitations' - early releases may not be balanced; (2) 'Clinical decision-making without validation' - research-only, requires clinical validation; (3) 'Re-identification attempts' - prohibited by license and ethics
sub_elements.quality_note: Three use constraints documented: awareness of ongoing enrollment imbalance, prohibition on unvalidated clinical use, and prohibition on re-identification attempts

sub_elements.name: Conflicts of Interest Declared
sub_elements.evidence: No 'ethics.conflicts_of_interest' field; no COI statement in ethical_reviews, human_subject_research, or other ethics sections
sub_elements.quality_note: Missing: No conflicts of interest declaration or statement present in metadata

sub_elements.name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
sub_elements.evidence: page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/2 (line 23); subsets section (line 208): 'Available at https://fairhub.io/datasets/2'; external_resources (lines 640-644): 'FAIRhub Dataset Landing Page: Dataset repository and download portal'
sub_elements.quality_note: Published on FAIRhub, a recognized platform for FAIR-compliant biomedical datasets with repository services and community engagement

sub_elements.name: Cross-referenced DOIs or Related Dataset Links
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources includes: (line 664) Zenodo archive with DOI 10.5281/zenodo.10642459; (line 668) BMJ Open protocol DOI 10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449; (line 673) Nature Metabolism commentary DOI 10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x; dataset DOI 10.57895/fairhub.2 (line 26)
sub_elements.quality_note: Multiple DOI cross-references: dataset DOI, Zenodo documentation archive, and peer-reviewed publications (BMJ Open protocol, Nature Metabolism) enabling citation and related resource discovery

sub_elements.name: Community Standards or Schema Reference
sub_elements.evidence: preprocessing_strategies (lines 440-448): 'OMOP Common Data Model for clinical data', 'DICOM for retinal imaging', 'mHealth standard for wearable device data', 'RxNorm codes for medications', 'ICD-10 codes for diabetes classification'
sub_elements.quality_note: Conformance to multiple community standards: OMOP CDM (clinical data harmonization), DICOM (medical imaging), mHealth (wearable devices), RxNorm (medication terminology), ICD-10 (diagnosis codes)

sub_elements.name: Associated Outreach Materials
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources section includes: (line 633) 'AI-READI Project Website' at https://aireadi.org/; (line 638) 'AI-READI Dataset Documentation' with version-specific guides at https://docs.aireadi.org/; (line 659) 'Data Sharing Information' at https://aireadi.org/goals/data-sharing; Zenodo archive (line 664) for additional documentation
sub_elements.quality_note: Comprehensive outreach materials: project website, version-specific documentation portal, data sharing policies, and Zenodo documentation archive

sub_elements.name: Similar Dataset Links or Thematic Grouping
sub_elements.evidence: keywords include 'Bridge2AI' (line 45); funders section (lines 180-186): 'NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI Program'; external_resources (lines 646-649): 'Bridge2AI Program: Parent NIH Common Fund program supporting AI-ready biomedical datasets https://bridge2ai.org/'
sub_elements.quality_note: Clear thematic grouping within Bridge2AI consortium of AI-ready biomedical datasets; link to parent program (https://bridge2ai.org/) enables discovery of related datasets (VOICE, CM4AI, CHORUS)

strengths: Excellent dataset discovery infrastructure with DOI (10.57895/fairhub.2), unique ID, comprehensive description, 20 keywords, and FAIRhub landing page
Strong access and distribution documentation: two-tier access model (public CC BY-NC 4.0, controlled DUA), file formats (DICOM, CSV, mHealth, XML), and comprehensive external resources (9 links)

Outstanding scientific motivation and funding transparency: NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI grant OT2OD032644 ($5M+), three clear purposes (salutogenesis, AI/ML standards, health equity), and Community Advisory Board involvement

Comprehensive data composition documentation: 4,000 participant target with triple-balanced design across race/ethnicity (4 groups) × sex (2) × diabetes severity (4), 10+ data modalities with detailed acquisition methods

Excellent cross-platform integration: FAIRhub publication, Bridge2AI consortium membership, OMOP/DICOM/mHealth/RxNorm/ICD-10 standards conformance, peer-reviewed publications (BMJ Open, Nature Metabolism)
Strong version tracking: documented release history (pilot May 2024, v1.0.0-v3.0.0), update schedule through November 2026, and versioned documentation at docs.aireadi.org

Comprehensive technical transparency: 3 sites (Birmingham, San Diego, Seattle), detailed device/manufacturer documentation for all modalities, extensive preprocessing documentation (harmonization, format conversion, QC)

Explicit limitations disclosure: volunteer selection bias and intentional minority over-sampling acknowledged; three discouraged uses documented (unvalidated clinical use, re-identification, early-data imbalance)
weaknesses: Missing deidentification documentation: no deidentification_and_privacy fields documenting method (HIPAA Safe Harbor, Expert Determination, k-anonymity) or examples of identifiers removed/masked
No processing code repositories: extensive device/tool documentation but no GitHub links, computational pipelines, or preprocessing code for full reproducibility
Missing identifier linking documentation: no identifiers_in_files field describing participant IDs, cross-file linking keys, or table join specifications
No top-level dataset version field: version history documented in updates section but no current version number in metadata header (e.g., dataset_version: 3.0.0)
Missing structured limitations section: limitations discussed in why_not_representative and discouraged_uses but no dedicated limitations field consolidating known issues
No conflicts of interest statement: no ethics.conflicts_of_interest field declaring potential COI for 20 creators or institutional relationships
No explicit ethical sourcing statement: bioethics guidance and Community Advisory Board mentioned but no formal ethics.ethical_position declaration
recommendations: Add deidentification_and_privacy section with approach field (e.g., 'HIPAA Safe Harbor with additional k-anonymity k=5') and examples_of_identifiers_removed list (dates shifted, names removed, geographic generalization, etc.)
Create software_and_tools section with preprocessing_code links to GitHub repositories for format conversion scripts, harmonization pipelines, and quality control code
Add data_characteristics.identifiers_in_files field documenting participant_id structure, linking keys across tables, and join specifications for multi-modal integration
Include top-level dataset_version field (e.g., version: 3.0.0) in metadata header with last_updated timestamp to clarify which release users are accessing

Add dedicated limitations field consolidating: (1) volunteer selection bias, (2) minority over-sampling vs. population prevalence, (3) ongoing enrollment imbalance in interim releases, (4) cross-sectional design limits causal inference

Include ethics.conflicts_of_interest field declaring any institutional, industry, or device manufacturer relationships (especially for imaging device vendors) or state 'No conflicts of interest declared'
Add ethics.ethical_position field with explicit statement on ethical data collection practices, Community Advisory Board role, health equity principles, and alignment with Bridge2AI ethical framework
